# Summary of the 2010 Liberal Democrat Manifesto

The 2010 Liberal Democrat Manifesto, titled "Change That Works for You – Building a Fairer Britain," presented a comprehensive platform centered on four core priorities: fair taxes, fair education, a green economy, and political reform.

## Tax Reform

The centerpiece proposal was raising the income tax threshold to £10,000, providing a £700 tax cut for most people and removing 3.6 million low earners from income tax entirely. This would be funded by taxing capital gains as income, restricting pension tax relief to the basic rate, introducing a 1% mansion tax on properties over £2 million, reforming non-domicile status, and converting Air Passenger Duty to a per-plane charge.

## Education

The party proposed a £2.5 billion "Pupil Premium" to support disadvantaged pupils through smaller class sizes and one-to-one tuition. They pledged to scrap university tuition fees within six years and replace the rigid National Curriculum with a slimmed-down framework giving schools greater autonomy.

## Economic and Environmental Policy

The manifesto outlined plans to create 100,000 jobs through green investment, including refurbishing shipyards for wind turbine manufacturing, an "Eco Cash-Back" scheme for home improvements, and bringing 250,000 empty homes back into use. A UK Infrastructure Bank would fund major projects. The party committed to breaking up banks to separate retail from investment banking and achieving carbon neutrality by 2050.

## Political Reform

Proposals included introducing proportional representation through the Single Transferable Vote system, establishing recall powers to remove corrupt MPs, capping donations at £10,000, creating an elected House of Lords, and drafting a written constitution. A Freedom Bill would restore civil liberties by scrapping ID cards, regulating CCTV, and protecting protest rights.

## Public Services

For the NHS, the party proposed cutting bureaucracy and reinvesting savings into frontline services, establishing elected Local Health Boards, and integrating health and social care. On policing, they pledged 3,000 additional officers funded by ID card savings.

## Other Priorities

The manifesto addressed immigration through regional points-based systems and restoring exit checks, supported armed forces through pay rises and housing improvements while opposing like-for-like Trident replacement, and committed to meeting the 0.7% GDP aid target. On Europe, they supported EU membership while calling for reform, and proposed an in/out referendum if fundamental treaty changes occurred.

The party acknowledged the deficit challenge, proposing savings of over £15 billion annually through measures including public sector pay caps, welfare reforms, and abolishing various quangos, with a Council on Financial Stability to oversee deficit reduction.
